scene: 1 — The supply base, before the emergency
detail: The narration's headline question is geographic — 'who is qualified to supply RUTF to north-east Nigeria today' — but the frame has no geography anywhere. 'Registry coverage by category' is commodity-only (RUTF 5 / Therapeutic milk 4 / Road transport 6 / Warehousing 2), and neither 'north-east Nigeria', 'Borno', nor 'four countries' appears in the captured viewport. A cold viewer gets counts, not the answer the voiceover promises. There is also no as-of stamp on a screen whose whole claim rests on the word 'today'.
fix_recommendation: Put the corridor/region axis on the opening frame: make 'Registry coverage' a commodity x corridor matrix (or add a corridor column), and stamp 'as of 28 Jul 2026' under the H1 so 'today' is literal.

scene: 1 — The supply base, before the emergency
detail: The dashboard surfaces a decision queue — '4 Applications to review / awaiting a decision' plus four named supplier rows — with no visible entry point into the decision. No Review button, no chevron, no link styling. The interaction is hand-waved at exactly the moment the user would act. (The same rows DO carry Review buttons one tab over in scene 2, so the affordance exists and is simply missing here.)
fix_recommendation: Give every 'Applications awaiting review' row a real affordance (a Review action or link-styled row with a hover state), and make the four KPI tiles and the coverage bars navigate to their filtered list.

scene: 1 — The supply base, before the emergency
detail: Three wrap defects in the 'Applications awaiting review' card: round names break mid-token ('OES Supply / Base 2026-' / 'B'), category chip text wraps to two lines INSIDE its pill border ('Therapeutic / milk'), and supplier names wrap to three lines ('Kano Therapeutic / Foods / PLC') with horizontal room available. The same chips render as clean single-line pills in scene 2, so this is a column-width bug specific to the dashboard card. Separately ~35% of the 'Registry coverage by category' card is dead whitespace (bars end ~y=425, card runs to ~y=655) because it is stretched to match the adjacent table card.
fix_recommendation: Set column min-widths and white-space: nowrap on round names and category chips (truncate + title tooltip if needed); either fill the coverage card's lower half with the corridor breakdown or let it size to content instead of stretching.

scene: 1 — The supply base, before the emergency
detail: The scene's concept_claim — answers 'who can supply RUTF to north-east Nigeria today' from one screen — is materially unshown. The corridor facet does not exist anywhere in the product, the RUTF row yields a count (5) and never a 'who', and 'four countries' appears nowhere in frame. The synthetic-data banner is present in the DOM but sits outside the captured viewport, so the opening frame carries no environment disclosure.
fix_recommendation: Either land the corridor facet on the dashboard (spine S0 already specifies 'per commodity AND per corridor', so the product is lagging its own design), or narrow scene 1's concept_claim to registry depth by commodity and let a later registry scene carry the corridor query.

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories
detail: The four declared categories ARE legible as chips on both round rows, so the concept_claim's substance is on screen. But the load-bearing half — 'every application arrives in the same shape and answers the same questions' — has no carrier: no form, no question set, no field list is visible anywhere. The columns shown (SUPPLIER/COUNTRY/ROUND/APPLIED FOR/SUBMITTED) are metadata any email inbox has. The narration also speaks 'ready-to-use therapeutic food' while the UI only ever prints the acronym RUTF, with no expansion, tooltip or legend.
fix_recommendation: Show the standardised application form once — even a read-only peek opened from a Review row — so 'the same questions' is visible rather than asserted; and expand the acronym once on screen (chip title or picker label: 'RUTF (ready-to-use therapeutic food)').

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories
detail: Action-fidelity failure. The narration asserts an effecting act — 'Ada OPENS a round and NAMES what they are collecting interest in' — but the action_trace is purely navigational: click .navitem('EOI rounds') -> wait_for .data-table -> hold 2.0s. There is no click on the 'New round' CTA (the most prominent control on the page, never touched), no fill of a round name, no category selection. The round being pointed at, OES Supply Base 2026-B, already existed and was already Open before the camera rolled — scene 1's dashboard reads '1 Open EOI rounds / 2 total'. Separately, the Rounds table says 2026-B has 8 APPLICATIONS while the Review queue shows exactly 4 rows, all 2026-B, with no filter chip, count, or pagination explaining the gap; and the closed 2026-A round's action cell is an inert em dash directly beneath a live Close button.
fix_recommendation: Add the effecting actions to the scene script: click 'New round', fill the round name, select all four categories, submit, and hold on the new row appearing in the Rounds table with its four chips. Separately label the Review queue as a filtered subset ('4 of 8 awaiting decision', linked to all 8) and replace the closed round's inert em dash with a real 'View results' action.

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories
detail: The mechanism (two-stage EOI-into-registry) traces cleanly to grounded spine S0 with two named documented sources. But the benefit actually narrated — 'every application answers the same questions' — is a step beyond what S0 documents (S0 is about a standing queryable supply base, not about question-set standardisation) and has no separate provenance link.
fix_recommendation: Either extend spine S0's evidence to cover the standardisation/comparability benefit by citing the documented EOI question-set requirement, or narrow the narration to what S0 actually documents and drop 'answers the same questions' until the question set is shown on screen.

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories
detail: The narrated act (opening and naming a round) has no footage, and 'answers the same questions' references a UI element — a question set — present nowhere in the screenshot or page text. The unexplained 8-applications-vs-4-queue-rows discrepancy is the first thing a careful reader asks about and is unanswered on screen.
fix_recommendation: Perform the create-round act on camera and surface the standardised question set once, so both narrated claims have on-screen carriers.

scene: 2 — Ada opens a round and names the categories
detail: Scripting/action-fidelity: the claimed multi-step declaration (create -> name -> declare categories) never occurred, so a viewer cannot tell from capture + trace that anything was declared. The camera work itself is clean — settled frame, no spinner, both tables fully unclipped, 2.0s hold — the framing is not the problem, the missing act is.
fix_recommendation: Script the effecting sequence (click New round -> fill name -> select x4 -> submit -> hold), timed so each category lands with the word that names it.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen
detail: The card's own copy does real work — 'What the reviewer is assessing / The profile frozen at submission, beside the live profile as it stands today' states the mechanic in plain language. But the 5-second read is wrong: the two prose columns are word-for-word IDENTICAL and occupy the largest type and biggest area in the frame, so the first impression is 'why am I reading the same paragraph twice — is this broken?'. The one element that actually demonstrates frozen-vs-live (UNICEF RUTF approval: 'expires Jul 1, 2027' vs 'UNICEF Supply Division (renewed) - expires Jul 27, 2028' + 'changed since') is in the smallest type at the modal's bottom edge.
fix_recommendation: Render the comparison as a diff, not two full copies: print the profile prose ONCE with a quiet 'unchanged' marker when both sides match, and promote the differing certification row to the top of the card.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen
detail: Action-fidelity failure. The narration is 'Amina applies for Savanna Nutrients, declaring capacity, the regions they can reach, and lead times per category. The moment they submit...' — the trace contains no fill, type, select or submit, only a nav click, a row click, a scroll_to and a hold. What is opened is OES Supply Base 2026-A, submitted Mar 12 2026, status Qualified: a PRIOR round's already-decided application. Worse, this creates a continuity break with the next scene: scene 4's review queue is entirely round 2026-B (Savanna submitted Jul 19), so the frozen snapshot the viewer is shown in scene 3 is NOT the submission Tomas reviews in scene 4. Both round labels are legible on screen ('OES Supply Base 2026-A — your application' vs '2026-B' on every queue row).
fix_recommendation: Seed a round Savanna has not yet applied to and drive the real apply form in-scene — fill capacity, regions, and a lead time per category, click Submit, then open the resulting submission's comparison card — so the freeze AT SUBMIT is on camera and the snapshot shown is the one the next scene reviews.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen
detail: Prominence inversion: the non-differentiating duplicate paragraph gets hero type while the single differing value gets the smallest type at the card's bottom edge, and the load-bearing explanatory sentence ('The reviewer's decision was made against the left-hand column, and editing the profile cannot reach it') sits flush on the modal's bottom boundary with no footer. Label drift inside one card: the prose block uses 'Frozen at submission' / 'Live profile today' while the table five lines below uses 'AS SUBMITTED' / 'LIVE TODAY' — four labels for two concepts. The modal is also scrolled so its own header block (status 'Qualified', 'Submitted Mar 12, 2026') is off the top, leaving an orphaned 'RUTF' chip at the frame edge.
fix_recommendation: Unify to one label pair across prose and table; collapse identical values with an 'unchanged' treatment; give the modal a footer so the explanatory line is not flush on the boundary; move the interpretive sentence behind an 'i' affordance on the card title.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen
detail: The application form, the capacity/regions/lead-time entry, and the submit control are nowhere in the frame. The immutability guarantee is asserted with nothing on screen an auditor could verify: no snapshot timestamp, no version/submission id, no link from the frozen copy to the decision it grounded. The 'changed since' chip carries no date. And the narration's hypothetical — 'if Savanna updates a certificate NEXT WEEK' — is spoken over a certificate that has already been renewed and flagged on screen.
fix_recommendation: Stamp the frozen column with its provenance ('Snapshot captured at submission - Mar 12, 2026 - submission #...') plus a link to the reviewer's decision record, and date the 'changed since' chip.

scene: 3 — Amina applies, and the profile is frozen
detail: The scroll_to + 3.0s hold landed the assessing card settled and fully in frame with the Commitments line visible — competently framed, no spinner, no blank frame. But the action sequence is not legible against the narration: the trace is navigate-and-open while the words describe a multi-step declare-and-submit operation, and the identity switch from Ada's procurement console to Savanna's supplier console happens between frames with no traced or narrated beat.
fix_recommendation: Once the apply act is scripted (see design_soundness), time the fill/submit beats to the words that name them; add a brief narrated or on-screen beat covering the persona handoff so the app does not silently change identity between cuts.

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry
detail: Neither half of the scene's concept_claim is present in the captured frame. The page text contains zero occurrences of 'Savanna', 'Qualified', 'Declined', 'expires', or any expiry date — the per-category split and the expiry, which ARE the scene, are both absent. What a viewer freezing on this frame reads is 'a review queue with three suppliers waiting'. The decided supplier simply vanishes; the only artifact of the decision is a content-free toast reading 'Decision recorded.' with no supplier, no categories, no outcomes, no expiry.
fix_recommendation: On 'Record decision', render the decided application as a persistent row on the same page (a 'Decided' group, or flip the row in place) reading 'Savanna Nutrients Ltd — RUTF: Qualified until 19 Jan 2028 - Therapeutic milk: Declined'. That one row puts the whole concept into the frame the viewer freezes on.

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry
detail: A core interaction is incoherent for a first-time user: recording a decision makes the object DISAPPEAR with no destination — no decided view, no link to the resulting qualification, no way to verify the expiry that was just set, no undo. Note this is NOT an action-fidelity failure: every effecting click (Qualify RUTF, Reject Therapeutic milk, Record decision) returned ok:true, so the demo genuinely performed the act. It is a result-legibility failure in the product.
fix_recommendation: Keep the decided item addressable: move it to a 'Decided' group on the same page carrying both per-category outcomes and a link to the supplier's qualification record, instead of removing it from the queue into nothing.

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry
detail: ~55% of the 720px viewport is empty white below the card (content ends at y~405) with nothing occupying it. The one confirmation moment — the toast — is marooned at (1180, 678), roughly 275px below the card's last row and diagonally opposite the table it changed; on a projector the eye is top-left and the confirmation will be missed. The APPLIED FOR chips are uniform inert grey pills with no state affordance, so the per-category concept is invisible in the resting table.
fix_recommendation: Let a decided-decision panel occupy the empty lower half; put the confirmation adjacent to the table it changed (inline row state) rather than as an orphan toast; give the APPLIED FOR chips semantic state (qualified / declined / pending).

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry
detail: Two rules fire together: the narrated expiry date appears nowhere in the captured page text, and the narration references the per-category qualify/decline stamp which is not present in the screenshot. The acts genuinely happened — the footage simply does not back them.
fix_recommendation: Surface granted/expires in the UI: name the supplier, both category outcomes, and the expiry in the confirmation text and in a persistent qualification row.

scene: 4 — Tomas qualifies the supplier, per category and with an expiry
detail: The narration is about the decision modal's per-category rows and the expiry they carry; the capture lands after 'Record decision' has dismissed that modal, so the narrated artifact is not clipped — it is entirely gone. The 2.2s post-toast hold guarantees the modal is long dismissed at frame time.
fix_recommendation: Move the settle-hold BEFORE the modal dismisses — capture the end-frame with both decision rows resolved (Qualified / Declined) and the expiry visible — or, once the persistent decided row lands, add a scroll_to + hold on that row after the toast.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: The subtitle states the concept in the product's own voice — 'Organisations holding live qualifications. Solicitations are issued from this registry' — and Savanna Nutrients Ltd correctly appears carrying RUTF with expiry Jan 19, 2028, so the previous scene's decision visibly landed. But the distinguishing half, 'current by construction', is invisible: the frame is indistinguishable from a hand-maintained directory. There is no denominator ('14 qualified' with no 'of 17 registered - 3 lapsed'), which is the one number that would prove derivation rather than maintenance.
fix_recommendation: Add a denominator line: '14 qualified - 1 lapsed in the last 30 days', with the lapsed org reachable so the removal is visible rather than narrated.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: Action-fidelity failure, unambiguous in the pixels. The narration says 'Ada FILTERS by commodity and country and gets an answer they can act on' — the trace is click .navitem('Supplier registry') -> wait_for -> hold 2.4s, with no select or click on any filter. All three controls read their defaults ('All categories' / 'All countries' / 'Any expiry') and the count reads the full '14 qualified suppliers'. The product plainly supports the filter and the demo never touches it. Separately, rows have no drill-in to the qualification the whole concept rests on, and the expiry select offers only 30/60/90-day windows with no 'expired/lapsed' state — so the question the concept_claim is built on cannot be asked of this product.
fix_recommendation: Add select actions on category=RUTF and country=Nigeria to scene 5's trace, timed to the words 'filters by commodity and country', holding on the result so the count visibly drops from 14 to the filtered number; and add an 'Expired / Lapsed' option plus a row drill-in to the underlying qualifications.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: The table is clipped at the fold — 'Volta Overland SARL' is cut mid-row at the viewport edge with no card bottom, footer or pagination, so a viewer cannot tell the list is complete. The QUALIFIED FOR badges are all one neutral grey even though the narration explicitly splits them ('these suppliers can make RUTF, these can move it') — commodity and service qualifications are visually indistinguishable. EARLIEST EXPIRY is an unexplained derived value: Kano Therapeutic Foods holds two qualifications and shows one date with no tooltip or 'i' bubble saying which one lapses then.
fix_recommendation: Split QUALIFIED FOR into two badge families (commodity vs service); add a card bottom/row count so completeness is legible; add an 'i' affordance on EARLIEST EXPIRY defining it as the minimum across a supplier's live qualifications.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: The mechanism traces to grounded spine S2 (Qualification model, org_can_bid — both implemented) and EARLIEST EXPIRY is the visible surface of that model. But the vivid second half of the narrated claim — a lapse removes a supplier, 'nobody had to remember' — has no provenance link to a demonstrated removal path, and the cited org_can_bid governs BID ELIGIBILITY, not registry membership: a semantic half-step beyond what the evidence supports.
fix_recommendation: Add evidence to S2 for the registry-membership derivation specifically (the query that excludes expired qualifications from GET /supply/api/registry/), rather than leaning on org_can_bid which governs a different gate.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: The scene's punchline — 'this one has dropped out because its certification lapsed last month' — has no referent anywhere. No lapsed, expired, struck-through or greyed supplier appears in the frame or page text; all 14 rows carry future expiries (earliest Oct 14, 2026). And the narrated filtered 'answer' is absent: the filters sit at defaults and the count reads the unfiltered 14.
fix_recommendation: Show the lapsed supplier rather than narrating it: an 'Expired / Lapsed' filter state rendering the dropped org greyed with its lapse date, so the absence the concept depends on becomes visible.

scene: 5 — The registry answers who can supply today
detail: The scene claims a filter interaction the trace never performs, so the narrated 'answer arriving' never happens on screen. Positives: no spinner, no blank frame, a 2.4s settle-hold on a fully painted page. Negatives beyond the action gap: the narrated table is clipped at the fold, and the persona swap from Reviewer/Tomas Berhane to Procurement/Ada Nwosu between frames reads as an unexplained jump cut.
fix_recommendation: Script the filter selects timed to the words, and hold on the filtered result; seat the table so its last row and card bottom are in frame.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: The scene's central claim — eligibility is enforced when the payload is built, so an unqualified supplier NEVER RECEIVES the solicitation — has zero on-screen evidence. There is no invitee list, no 'issued to N qualified suppliers', no qualification badge on any bidder, and no supplier-side view. The viewer takes the entire claim on the narrator's word, on a screen that is in fact a price comparison table. The narrated specifics DO land verbatim ('60,000 cartons RUTF delivered to Maiduguri ... due Sep 15, 2026') and the arithmetic checks (60,000 x 42.29 = 2,537,400), which is what keeps this at 3.
fix_recommendation: Show the NEGATIVE case: the walkthrough already switches persona, so cut to a supplier holding only a non-matching qualification (Maiduguri Cold Chain Stores — Warehousing only, or Sahel Milk Products SARL — Therapeutic milk only) and show this solicitation ABSENT from their list, beside a qualified supplier's list where it appears. That is the only framing that shows 'never receives it' rather than 'button hidden'.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: Action-fidelity failure, and the screen actively contradicts the narrated act. The narration says 'Ada PUBLISHES a solicitation'; the trace is click Solicitations -> click 'Compare bids' -> scroll_to -> hold. No publish occurs, and the solicitation is already in state 'Published' with 15 priced bids across 4 lots — a publication cannot be watched here. Independently, four identical filled primary Award buttons per lot (8+ on screen) present a $2.9M irreversible commitment as one of four equal-weight clicks, with no confirm step and no leader marked, under a blank action-column header.
fix_recommendation: Either open on the solicitation BEING published (the compose/publish step, where the eligibility scope is chosen and an issue-set count appears) and leave bid comparison to scene 7, or change the narration to describe what is on screen.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: The mouse cursor occludes a load-bearing figure — Maiduguri row 2 renders as 'USD 2,#6,200.00' (page text confirms USD 2,626,200.00) — an unreadable number in a $2.6M bid table. TECHNICAL scores (91/60/83/82) are all the same brand green regardless of value, styled like links with no affordance cue: decorative, not semantic. Money columns are left-aligned with '.00' cents on seven-figure values, so magnitudes do not align by column shape. The Award column header is blank while every other column is labelled. The frame terminates mid-row on the Djibo lot with a half-clipped button.
fix_recommendation: Park the cursor off the data columns before the hold; right/decimal-align UNIT PRICE and LOT VALUE and drop cents on LOT VALUE; label the action column; render TECHNICAL as '91/100' with an 'i' bubble carrying the rubric and scorer; end the scroll on a card boundary.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: Three narrated UI states — 'visible only to suppliers holding a live qualification', 'an unqualified supplier's page never receives the solicitation', 'shown it with the button hidden' — none of which appear in the screenshot or page text. Offsetting credit: the narrated lot quantities, destination and delivery date are on screen verbatim and the arithmetic checks out, which is why this is a 2 and not a 1.
fix_recommendation: Put the eligibility rule on screen (issue-set count, or the negative supplier-side case) so the claim has a carrier.

scene: 6 — A solicitation reaches only qualified suppliers
detail: Scene 6 and scene 7 are the SAME modal roughly 135px of scroll apart, with content-identical page text. Two consecutive scenes spend their screen time on one payload: scene 6 borrows scene 7's subject (per-lot bid comparison) and has none of its own, so the demo visibly stalls. Compounded by the cursor occluding a bid value and the frame terminating mid-row.
fix_recommendation: Give scene 6 its own subject and its own frame — script it on the publish/eligibility surface — leaving the per-lot bid tables entirely to scene 7.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: The concept genuinely lands in the data — Savanna leads Maiduguri at 42.29 and Faso leads Djibo at 41.85, both visible in one frame with Savanna dropping to second — and the modal's own brief says 'Bid lot by lot — OES intends to award corridors separately'. What holds it at 3: the top table has NO title in the scored frame (the 'Maiduguri' heading is scrolled off, leaving only a half-cut subtitle line), and the price-rank rule is unstated — rows are price-ascending but there is no sort indicator, so the viewer must take both the lot identity and the ranking on faith.
fix_recommendation: Add a sticky per-lot header so the lot name stays pinned while its bids scroll, plus an explicit sort indicator on UNIT PRICE ('ranked by unit price').

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: In the TECHNICAL column, 7 of the 15 bids on this surface (all four Damaturu rows and all three haulage rows) render the literal word 'Score' — an action — in the same green treatment as a real value (91 / 60 / 83 / 82), under a header that says neither 'score' nor 'action'. A first-time user cannot tell whether that is a missing value, a button, or a bug. Separately the # rank column implies a decision rule the screen never states while displaying a technical score that demonstrably does not feed it (Kano at 60 outranks Lagos at 83).
fix_recommendation: Render the unscored state as a visibly distinct secondary action (outline button, '+ Score bid', grey not green), rename the header to 'TECHNICAL SCORE', and label the rank column with its actual basis.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: The modal scrim is too light: six background 'Compare bids' buttons are clipped mid-word and remain saturated down the right edge, competing with the eight Award buttons inside the modal, and nav labels behind read legibly. The two lot tables do not share a column grid (UNIT PRICE at x~481 vs x~487, LOT VALUE 601 vs 607) — misalignment on exactly the axis the scene asks you to compare across. Content scrolls under the sticky modal header with no mask or fade, leaving a half-cut line of text pinned at the top edge so the frame reads mid-scroll rather than settled. Money is left-aligned rather than decimal-aligned.
fix_recommendation: Darken the backdrop scrim; share one column grid across all lot tables; right/decimal-align UNIT PRICE and LOT VALUE and move 'USD' to the header; mask or fade content under the sticky header.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: The load-bearing claim IS fully verifiable in frame — the leader on Maiduguri is not the leader on Djibo, visible without being told. But the secondary clause 'with the reviewer's technical score beside each one' is false on this very surface: 7 of 15 bids carry no score, and 'the reviewer's' has no referent anywhere — no scorer identity, date, or methodology is shown.
fix_recommendation: Either score the remaining two lots in the fixture, or narrow the narration to 'the technical score the review panel recorded for these two lots'.

scene: 7 — Bids priced and scored lot by lot
detail: Fits-but-mis-framed: the narration explicitly names 'the Maiduguri lot' while that lot's own heading is clipped off the top of the frame — roughly 40px less scroll would have seated it. The still also lands looking mid-scroll (half-cut line under the sticky header) with the cursor sitting on a Djibo lot value. Pacing itself is good: real effecting click, all trace entries ok:true, 2.4s and 2.6s holds, and a legible before/after change matching the narration's move between cards.
fix_recommendation: Adjust the scroll_to offset so the Maiduguri card header is seated before the beat that names it, and park the cursor off the data before the capture hold.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: The frame is excellent and the mechanic lands in five seconds — 'Awarded — Savanna Nutrients Ltd' and 'Awarded — Faso NutriWorks SA' on two lots of one tender, with the parent counter moving 0/4 to 2/4. But the narrated WHY IT MATTERS is refuted by the tables directly beneath it. Narration: 'Splitting costs a little more per carton.' On screen: the split total is 60,000 x 42.29 + 20,000 x 41.85 = USD 3,374,400 (blended 42.1800/carton). Every single-source alternative is MORE expensive: Savanna both lots 3,455,400 (+81,000, +1.0125/carton), Kano both 3,554,600 (+180,200), Lagos both 3,693,600 (+319,200), Faso both 3,755,400 (+381,000). The split is the global cost MINIMUM — it is 1.0125/carton CHEAPER than the best consolidation, not dearer. The premise fails too: single-sourcing here is both more expensive AND more fragile, so the demo shows a free lunch while narrating a sacrifice. The named domain expert does this subtraction in about three seconds.
fix_recommendation: Replace the trade-off sentence with the honest, stronger one this fixture actually supports — each corridor's own cheapest bidder is a different plant, so the split is simultaneously the resilient AND the lowest-cost award — OR re-price Faso's Djibo bid above Savanna's so a genuine premium exists to narrate. Recommend the narration edit; the data edit is the alternative.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: Scored once for the WHOLE walkthrough and attached here as the most emblematic scene. The domain is genuinely load-bearing — a USD 3.37M, 80,000-carton, two-country lean-season tender in the real UNICEF/WFP two-stage shape — and no toy-input rule fires. But the walkthrough repeatedly exercises the feature where its value is LEAST felt: 14 suppliers and a 3-row review queue (a spreadsheet handles that), registry filters never used, eligibility never demonstrated on the negative case, and the headline 'deliberate split' turning out to be nothing more than awarding each lot to its own cheapest bidder — the trivial case, not the interesting one. Nothing in the product helps Ada split ON PURPOSE rather than by price reflex, which is exactly what the narration claims is happening. A skeptic reasonably asks 'so the feature is that the Award button is per-lot?'
fix_recommendation: Demonstrate the feature where its value is actually felt: add a supplier-concentration/exposure signal (share of tender value and cartons per supplier, per corridor) so the split reads as a deliberate risk decision, and walk lots where price and technical DISAGREE so the comparison changes an answer. This changes what is demonstrated, so it is a narrative decision, not a polish pass.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: The interaction loop is clean and fully coherent — click, badge, toast, counter, buttons retire — and both awards genuinely fired on camera (all trace entries ok:true). What holds it at 3: a USD 2.5M award fires on ONE click with no confirmation, no captured rationale, and no revoke path afterwards; and the # rank implies a decision rule the screen never states while displaying a TECHNICAL score that demonstrably does not feed it.
fix_recommendation: Add a confirm step that records an award rationale, actor and timestamp on the lot, surface it on the awarded badge, add a revoke action, and label the rank column with its actual basis.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: The modal scrim is too light — background page buttons ('olicitation', six 'mpare bids') remain fully legible and clipped mid-word down the right third. The toast occludes live content: the ' 35,000 cartons RUTF delivered to Damaturu' card header is covered at the bottom edge. TECHNICAL scores are uniform brand green regardless of value (60 renders identically to 91) — decorative, not semantic. After award, the trailing button column collapses so awarded and unawarded lot tables no longer share geometry. Seven-figure lot values carry '.00' cents.
fix_recommendation: Darken the scrim; offset the toast above the card stack; make TECHNICAL encode an objective stated threshold or render it plain; reserve the action-column width post-award.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: The concept_claim traces cleanly to spine S4 ('award is per-lot, so one tender can be split across suppliers and corridors on purpose') and the scene demonstrates exactly that — provenance intact and uncontradicted. But the narration layers on an economic assertion — a per-carton premium, 'buys the thing money cannot buy later' — that appears NOWHERE in the why_brief: S4's rationale is entirely about corridor concentration risk and never mentions cost. One narrated claim with no traceable provenance, and it happens to be the one the data refutes.
fix_recommendation: Drop the unsupported cost clause from the narration, or add a grounded spine item covering the cost-of-resilience economics with real evidence before asserting it on camera.

scene: 8 — Two suppliers, two corridors, one tender
detail: Not a 1: the primary claim — two lots, two suppliers, awarded on camera — is fully evidenced by both badges, the toast, and the 0/4 to 2/4 counter. It is a 2 because the scene's interpretive claim is not merely unshown but ACTIVELY REFUTED by the page's own numbers, by USD 81,000. Compounding: the screen shows no total anywhere, so a USD 3,374,400 award decision is presented as two unsummed tables and the viewer is asked to reach a cost conclusion the product never computes.
fix_recommendation: Fix the narration (preferred) or the bid book, and add an award-summary line (total awarded value, blended per-carton price, supplier exposure) so the cost claim is checkable on screen either way.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The in-panel copy is above average — 'Drawn against / The appropriation this contract obligates money from' and 'Delivery schedule / The consignments this contract is moving on' define each block in plain language — so an outsider gets 'contract -> money source -> shipments'. But the concept the scene exists to demonstrate, the award-to-contract handover, has NO on-screen carrier, so the 5-second read is not merely incomplete, it is wrong: continuity from the previous scene tells the viewer this is the 60,000-carton award they just watched.
fix_recommendation: Add a first-class provenance line to the contract header, above 'Drawn against': 'Awarded from: RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q2 2026 - Lot: 45,000 cartons RUTF delivered to Maiduguri - awarded <date>', rendered as a clickable backlink to the awarded lot.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: Three coherence failures at once. (a) The contract modal is a dead end in the one direction the concept requires: searching the full page text for 'RUTF Northeast Nigeria Q3 2026', 'solicitation', 'award', 'lot' or 'tender' returns nothing — the record traces DOWN to money and FORWARD to consignments, but the upward link to the award is the only one absent (and execution.py already models Contract-from-Award, so the relation exists in code and is simply not serialised). (b) The drill-down does not resolve the anomaly it surfaced: you click a Pipeline row reading SHIPPED 54,910 against a 45,000-carton requirement and land on a modal that never mentions 54,910. That figure is a multi-hop leg double-count — hub-to-centre legs sum to 9,910 and upstream legs (20,000 + 15,000 + 10,000) to 45,000, giving exactly 54,910, so the same cartons are counted two and three times in a product whose pitch is carton-level traceability. (c) The output contradicts its own label: 'DISBURSED USD 842,000.00 - AGAINST CONFIRMED DELIVERY ONLY' equals exactly 20,000 cartons at 42.10, while the same modal's footer confirms 44,675 cartons at destination.
fix_recommendation: Serialise the Award foreign key into the contract payload and render an explicit Award -> Contract -> Consignments chain in the modal; fix SHIPPED to count terminal delivery legs only (or label it 'leg-movements' and add a distinct cartons-shipped measure); and make DISBURSED self-explaining inline ('USD 842,000.00 - 20,000 of 44,675 confirmed cartons invoiced').

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The modal is clipped mid-row at the bottom edge and underlying page content occupies the same pixels as the SHP-2026-0908 row (a green pill and a 'Tag' fragment bleed through) — a frame element occluding content. There is no visible scroll affordance, so 11 of 16 consignments and the single most load-bearing sentence on the screen ('45,000 cartons contracted - 44,675 confirmed at destination - 325 outstanding. Status and quantities are derived from the event log, not entered.') are unreachable in the frame. The 'Drawn against' grid has a dead two-column hole beside UNIT PRICE where row 2 fails to reflow, with the cursor parked in the void. The load-bearing qualifier 'AGAINST CONFIRMED DELIVERY ONLY' is the smallest, lowest-contrast text on the panel, and the QUANTITY column is left-aligned. The IATI field renders a doubled segment: US-GOV-1-OES-OES-C-2026-NG1.
fix_recommendation: Give the modal a proper scroll container with a visible affordance and a sticky footer pinning the reconciliation line; right-align QUANTITY; promote the confirmed-delivery qualifier to a readable caption; let the 'Drawn against' grid reflow; fix the IATI identifier concatenation.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: Spine S5 is grounded (design spec §1 documented; execution.py Contract-from-Award-drawing-on-Appropriation implemented) and the APPROPRIATION half of the claim is fully demonstrated — funder, appropriation, IATI activity, obligated 1,894,500 (= 45,000 x 42.10, internally consistent), disbursed never exceeding obligated. But the 'same record the tender produced' half is asserted in narration with no on-screen link, so the claim the scene exists to prove is the one it does not evidence.
fix_recommendation: Either drive the scene off the contract the on-camera award actually produced so quantity and price carry through unchanged and 'immutable' is literally demonstrated, or keep the Q2 contract and say so in narration while adding the on-screen 'Awarded from' line. This needs a pick — whether the first option is buildable at capture time is not determinable from the artifacts.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: ANSWERS THE OPEN QUESTION (a): the framing is NOT honest on camera. The recipe's authoring note knows this is the earlier Q2 contract, but that note is never spoken and never rendered — and the note itself asserts the false identity ('the contract the Maiduguri award became'). The viewer has just watched a 60,000-carton Maiduguri lot awarded to Savanna at 42.29 and is now shown a Savanna/Maiduguri contract for 45,000 cartons at 42.10, with no explanation. A buyer reads that as either the 'immutable' award being silently mutated (-25% quantity, -0.19/carton) on the very frame that word is spoken, or a partial contract at a renegotiated price with no amendment record. A third tell settles it: the delivery schedule contains 12 consignments already Delivered between Jul 11-21 2026 plus SHP-2026-0302 delivered Jul 27, all BEFORE the award just made (the dashboard's runs-dry date puts today at Jul 28, 2026). A contract created by that award cannot have completed deliveries a fortnight earlier.
fix_recommendation: Add the on-screen 'Awarded from' backlink AND one narration clause naming the source ('this one came from the Q2 award into the same corridor, already in execution'), so the quantity and price change is self-explaining instead of reading as a faked link.

scene: 9 — The award becomes the contract
detail: The sequence is legible end-to-end, every trace entry is ok:true, the effecting click lands a real result frame, and the 1.6s pre-click hold gives the Pipeline table time to read. Rough edges: the narration's second clause names the delivery schedule while only 4.5 of 16 rows are on screen, and the 3.2s hold sits on a static clipped frame that never scrolls to the reconciliation line that is the scene's actual proof; and the hard cut from award-modal to contract-modal falls exactly where continuity is implied but not shown.
fix_recommendation: During the 3.2s hold, scroll inside the modal to its footer so '45,000 contracted - 44,675 confirmed at destination - 325 outstanding - derived from the event log, not entered' is on screen as the narration says 'the same record is what the supply chain moves against'.
